messages:
alex.w: Hey team — emergency dental extraction while Im in Santorini for a conference. Clinic pulled a tooth and charged €250. They say they can do direct billing only with a 'guarantee of payment' or company authorization form. I paid in cash. Can People Ops issue a temporary proof of coverage / authorization I can hand them so they don't charge me again? Also need to know what to file for HSA reimbursement.

leo.benefits: Oof hope youre okay, teeth suck. We typically dont issue guarantees of payment directly to providers, but we can create a proof-of-coverage letter with policy number, claim intake email/phone, and a short note authorizing the provider to contact the insurer for verification. That usually convinces billing desks.

claims_bot: Automated claim guidance: Submit dental/out-of-network expenses at https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "International reimbursement". Required: itemized invoice, proof of payment (receipt or bank/card statement), date of service, provider name and tax ID (if available). File types: pdf/png/jpg. Expected processing: 2-6 weeks depending on documentation.

leo.benefits: Quick checklist for what to hand the clinic: 1) proof-of-coverage letter (we can generate), 2) a copy/photo of your Redwood digital benefits card (we can include policy #), 3) itemized invoice with procedure codes or description, and 4) copy of passport or boarding pass if this was work travel.

alex.w: They want an English invoice or at least an English summary of line items. The clinic only has Greek originals. Will an English note from us plus the Greek invoice be ok?

jon.claims: Yes, include both. For international dental claims we accept the original plus an English translation or summary. If you submit for HSA reimbursement, include a receipt showing paid amount and diagnosis/procedure. HSA rules: eligible medical expenses must be substantiated; HSA may reimburse net of VAT in some countries. Keep your card statement showing the charge date/currency.

leo.benefits: I'll draft the letter. Copy/paste this to the clinic if they ask for a company contact: 
```
Redwood Inference - Benefits Claims
Policy #: RW-PL-2039
Claims intake: claims@redwood.com
Phone (intl support): +1-800-555-0199 (Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 CET)
Please contact claims@redwood.com to confirm coverage details for patient Alex W. We confirm the above-named employee is an active plan member. This letter is for verification only and not a guarantee of payment.
```

sophia.hr: If this was work-related (conference), upload the boarding pass or calendar invite with travel dates when you file and mark the claim "business travel". That flags it for expedited review. Also please DM me the clinic contact if you want me to call and confirm receipt of the letter.

alex.w: Thanks. One more: can you note on the letter that the company authorizes the clinic to bill the insurer directly if possible? Theyre saying they need that exact phrase.

leo.benefits: I can add a short line: "The employer authorizes the provider to contact the insurer for verification and direct billing where insurer policy allows." I will not phrase it as an unconditional guarantee.

jon.claims: When you file, attach a screenshot of the currency conversion for the date (OANDA or card exchange). That speeds accounting. Also keep originals in case insurer requests certified translations.

alex.w: Uploading the invoice and passport pic to the portal now. Appreciate the fast help.

leo.benefits: Sent you the PDF letter in DM, includes insurer contacts and the phrase you asked for. Hand it to billing and ask them to email claims@redwood.com with their invoice. Ill also mark the claim urgent.

sophia.hr: Follow-up: if direct billing is refused, submit for reimbursement via portal and choose expedited processing + attach travel proof. For HSA submission, save the itemized receipt and card statement.

alex.w: Clinic accepted the letter and will email claims@redwood.com. Thanks everyone, pain gone and back to sessions :relieved:
